mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next month will increase weekday downtown traffic and convert more trips into retail visits, pushing RETAIL_REC higher than in the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both less depressed than retail but still far below baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not each rise above their t-0w levels for most of the next 4 weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below the prior 4-week mean despite such rises, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL time remains elevated and WORKPLACES stay depressed, commuters and households substitute away from discretionary shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 while WORKPLACES stays below -50
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative throughout t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 and WORKPLACES stays below -50 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC does not weaken relative to the prior two-week average, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold drop in TRANSIT below its recent already-low level signals renewed access frictions or service cutbacks, which suppress retail visits with about a one-week lag and lowers RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is near -61 to -64 across the snapshot and remains materially below baseline
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -65 and RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week relative to the prior week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A relative rise in PARKS mobility, especially when GROCERY_PHARM is stable, indicates outdoor-oriented activity substitution that diverts time and spending away from retail corridors, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM fluctuate around roughly -30 while RETAIL_REC stays near -65 to -71
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while GROCERY_PHARM remains roughly flat and RETAIL_REC still increases over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent narrowing of the gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies more commuting and more en-route purchases, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved from t-3w to t-0w relative to their lows
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior two-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM strengthens while RETAIL_REC remains weak, households are reallocating errands to essential trips instead of discretionary shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to stay flat or fall over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is less depressed than RETAIL_REC in every observed week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above -25 and RETAIL_REC increases over the following 28 days relative to the previous 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals reduced city-center access and lower daytime footfall, which depresses RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:both remain around the low -60s and low -50s at the decision time
failure_condition: If, under tightening restrictions, TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not fall together or RETAIL_REC does not weaken within one week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS coupled with stable RESIDENTIAL time reflects warmer-weather substitution toward local outdoor activity, which pulls discretionary time away from retail and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -28 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +15
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is near -26 to -31 while RESIDENTIAL is consistently positive near +16 to +17
failure_condition: If PARKS rises above -28 with RESIDENTIAL above +15 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior two-week average, the hypothesis is rejected.
